title: Shopify Shop MCP: What Your Product Data Now Has to Carry
summary: Shopify's Shop MCP lets any AI agent search and buy from Shopify Catalog. What agents filter on, what Shopify fills in for you and what to fix first.
body_markdown:
On 13 October 2026, Shopify[launched Shop MCP](https://shopify.dev/changelog/posts/add-shopping-and-shop-pay-checkout-to-any-agent-with-shop-mcp) , one connection that lets an AI agent search Shopify Catalog, build a cart and check out. Shopify Catalog holds more than a billion products, and search needs no API key.


For merchants, the change is reach. Eligible products are in Shopify Catalog automatically, so any agent that connects can find them. What it finds is whatever your[product data](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/product-data-for-ai-shopping-agents) says.


## What is Shopify Shop MCP?


Shop MCP is a hosted server, at mcp.shop.com, that any agent supporting the Model Context Protocol can connect to. According to[Shop's developer docs](https://shop.dev/docs/) , it exposes 17 tools that cover search and product details, carts and checkout, and order tracking.


The catalog, cart and checkout data follow Google's[Universal Commerce Protocol](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/google-ucp-what-it-is-and-why-it-matters-for-ecommerce) , one of the[agentic commerce protocols](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/acp-vs-ucp-vs-mcp-vs-ap2) alongside ACP and MCP.


## How does Shop Pay work with Shop MCP?


Shop Pay is how a shopper pays without leaving the agent. According to[Shop's checkout docs](https://shop.dev/docs/checkout) , there are three ways a purchase completes:


- **Not signed in.** The agent builds the cart and opens a checkout, then sends the shopper to the merchant's checkout page to enter delivery and payment details.
- **Signed in with Shop.** Saved addresses fill in delivery, and the merchant can offer Shop Pay. The agent completes the checkout only after the shopper approves the purchase and chooses how to pay. The docs tell agents to "never pick a default" payment method.
- **A store that isn't on Shopify.** The shopper approves the purchase in Shop with a spending limit, and Shop issues card details for that one purchase, which the agent uses on the store's own checkout. Shop calls these[spend requests](https://shop.dev/docs/approvals) .


For a Shopify merchant, an agent order arrives like any other order, paid through Shop Pay or the store's own checkout.


## How is Shop MCP different from Shopify's earlier AI channels?


Shopify already sent catalog data to named AI platforms, such as ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, through its agentic storefronts. Shop MCP opens the same catalog to any agent that connects, with no partnership needed.


That makes Shopify Catalog closer to public infrastructure for[agentic commerce](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/agentic-commerce) . A shopping assistant built by a startup gets the same search as one built by a large AI platform.


## How are Amazon, Shopify and Walmart handling AI shopping agents?


On 21 September 2026, Amazon[blocked Meta's Muse agent](https://www.thekeyword.co/news/amazon-blocks-meta-muse-agent) from buying on Amazon.com, about two weeks after Muse launched. Shoppers who tried saw a message that continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use. Amazon said agents that buy for customers "should operate openly and respect service provider decisions", and that Muse never asked permission and doesn't identify itself while browsing. Amazon runs its own shopping agents through Alexa.


Shopify went the other way. The same day, it said Muse could complete purchases in Shopify stores with Shop Pay. Shopify says agents used to find products and then send shoppers to the store's site to pay, which "often caused drop-off". Shop MCP keeps payment inside the agent and extends that to any agent that connects.


On 21 October, Walmart[opened Walmart and Sam's Club to approved agents](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/21/while-amazon-blocks-ai-agents-walmart-rolls-out-the-welcome-mat/) through its own MCP server, with per-agent spending limits for shoppers and a block on agents that don't follow its terms.


Our read: the large platforms are splitting into stores that keep agents out and stores that let them in on their own terms. For merchants, that means:


- **Reach goes to open stores.** An agent that can't check out on one site can still recommend products it can buy somewhere else.
- **Control moves to the terms.** Open stores set the rules agents follow, such as Walmart's spending limits or Shopify's shopper approval before payment, instead of blocking agents outright.
- **Product data decides who gets picked.** When every Shopify merchant is reachable through the same search, an agent chooses between them on what the product data says.


## Are your products included in Shop MCP?


If your store and products are eligible, they're in Shopify Catalog automatically. Shopify's[Catalog help page](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog) says you can't opt out of the Catalog itself. You can stop individual agentic storefronts from accessing your products, and the products stay in the Catalog for other uses. As of launch week, Shopify's merchant help pages don't mention Shop MCP by name.


Shopify's[eligibility requirements](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog/requirements) set a low bar for each product:


- A title and at least one product image
- A price above zero
- Published to your online store, and not unlisted or hidden from search engines
- Not in an excluded category


The excluded list covers categories like alcohol, weapons and event tickets. It also includes uncategorized products. A product without a category isn't in the Catalog, so no agent can find it. Shopify also notes that its own classification can differ from the category you set in admin, and that complete product information helps it classify correctly.


## How do AI agents search products through Shop MCP?


An agent searches by[text, a similar product or a photo](https://shop.dev/docs/search) . It can then narrow results with filters, and Shopify's docs call these hard requirements: a product that fails any filter isn't returned.


The filters include:


- **Attributes:** size, color and target gender
- **Price:** a minimum and maximum
- **Shipping:** where the product ships to and from
- **Category:** taxonomy category IDs
- **Rating:** for example, at least 4 stars from at least 20 reviews
- **Availability:** buyable items only, by default


Take a home textiles brand selling a cotton sheet set. A shopper asks an agent for a queen sheet set in sage green under $150 that ships to Texas. If the set's sizes and colors are variant options named Size and Color, the agent's filters have values to match. If the color only appears in the product title, or the variants are labeled "Option 1", the filter has nothing to match against.


An independent test of Shopify Catalog search by[No Hacks](https://nohacks.co/blog/shopify-products-more-reviews-come-back-higher) , run over 1,305 searches in launch week, found that filters such as target gender and price replaced 8 to 9 of the top 10 results. It also found that products with more reviews tended to rank higher, and that one-word changes in the query, such as "unscented" vs "fragrance-free", changed the top 10. Shopify doesn't publish how it ranks results.


## What product data do agents get from Shopify Catalog?


Shopify's[Global Catalog docs](https://shopify.dev/docs/agents/catalog/global-catalog) list what each result can carry:


- Title, description, product URL and images
- Categories, using Google's product category and the merchant's own taxonomy
- Options and variants, with SKU, price and availability for each variant
- Ratings, with the review count
- Attributes, tech specs, top features and selling points


Shopify infers several of these fields itself, including the description, options, attributes, tech specs and top features. The docs describe the inferred fields as discovery and merchandising signals, not merchant-authored text.


So when your product data is thin, an agent still gets an answer about your product. It's Shopify's reading of the product, though, not yours. The No Hacks test found ingredient lists on 36 of 50 merchant product pages it checked, but in the catalog text for only 5 of them.


## What should you fix in your Shopify catalog first?


Shopify's own guidance on[optimizing products for AI platforms](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-catalog/optimizing-products) asks for clear, accurate and detailed product information. For the sheet set, that turns into five checks:


1. **Give every product a category.** Uncategorized products are excluded from the Catalog. Set the category in Shopify's product taxonomy, not only in a tag or a collection.
2. **Put size and color in variant options.** Name the options Size and Color, and keep values consistent across products, so "Queen" is never also "Qn" or "Queen size".
3. **Add barcodes.** Shopify asks for barcodes such as UPCs and GTINs, and agents can look up a product directly by its GTIN or UPC.
4. **Write the specs into the description.** Material, thread count, weave and care instructions should be in the text, so an agent doesn't have to infer them.
5. **Keep store policies complete.** Agents answer questions such as "can I return this?" from your policies.


Then test what an agent sees. Shopify's shop command-line tool runs the same catalog search an agent uses, so you can search for your own products the way a shopper would.


## What hasn't Shopify said about Shop MCP yet?


A few things merchants will want to know aren't in Shopify's documentation yet:


- **Fees.** Shopify hasn't published whether Shop MCP sales carry any charge beyond standard payment processing.
- **Opting out.** The controls for individual agentic storefronts don't mention Shop MCP.
- **Analytics.** Agent orders appear in your Shopify admin like other orders. The purchase never loads your storefront, so site analytics and ad pixels don't record a visit.


Each checkout also belongs to one merchant, so a basket from three stores becomes three checkouts.

## FAQs


### Can I opt out of Shop MCP?


Shopify says you can't opt out of Shopify Catalog. You can stop individual agentic storefronts from accessing your products, but Shopify hasn't said whether those controls apply to Shop MCP.


### Do merchants need to set anything up for Shop MCP?


Shopify's launch notes describe no merchant setup. Eligible products are in Shopify Catalog automatically, and agent orders appear in your Shopify admin.


### Is Shop Pay required for Shop MCP?


No. Without Shop sign-in, the shopper pays on the merchant's own checkout page. Signed-in shoppers can pay with Shop Pay inside the agent, once they approve the purchase.


### Does Shop MCP charge merchants a fee?


Shopify hasn't published merchant fees for Shop MCP sales.


### Is Shop MCP the same as the Shopify Dev MCP server?


No. Shopify's Dev MCP server helps developers build apps and themes. Shop MCP is for shopping: it lets agents search Shopify Catalog, build carts and check out.
